stem:
Meena lowers a metal bucket into a bucket of water in her kitchen.
She notices that the bucket feels much lighter inside the water than in the air, even though she is holding it the same way.
Why does the bucket feel lighter in the water?

options.text: The water removes the force of gravity acting on the bucket.
The water pushes the bucket upward with a force equal to the weight of water it displaces.
The mass of the bucket decreases when it enters the water.
The air inside the bucket makes it float like a balloon.

teacher.key_rationale: An immersed object experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the liquid displaced; this upward force partly balances gravity, so the object feels lighter while gravity still acts. Only B states this correctly.
